en.name: AGrammarly: Reply Helper
en.title: AGrammarly — Reply Helper
en.subtitle: On-device reply suggestions
en.short_description: Suggested replies that sound like you. Runs on your device. No account, no ads.
en.description:
AGrammarly suggests replies to the messages you get, and it does the whole job on your phone.

—— How it works ——

Paste or type the message you received. AGrammarly offers three replies to choose from — one casual, one professional, one short — ranked by how well they fit. Tap one to use it.

Suggestions come from a pattern set that ships inside the app, combined with the phrasings and emoji you use most. There is no model call and no server: the matching runs on the device, so it works with no signal at all.

—— It learns how you write ——

The more replies you accept, the more your own phrasing shows up in what it offers. Your most-used emoji move to the front. All of that is stored on your device, and Settings can delete every bit of it in one action.

—— A practice keyboard ——

The Keyboard tab is a full QWERTY layout inside AGrammarly with the suggestion bar above it, so you can try the flow and see the keystrokes it saves. It is a practice surface inside this app — AGrammarly does not install a system keyboard, so it does not appear in your keyboard list for use in other apps.

—— What it keeps ——

No account. No sign-up. No advertising SDK and no analytics SDK. Nothing you type leaves the phone, because there is nowhere for it to go: this build ships with no suggestions service configured. Your learned style and your counters live on the device and nowhere else.

—— Honest about what it is not ——

AGrammarly is a reply helper, not a grammar or spelling checker, and not a writing assistant powered by a language model. It suggests replies; it does not correct your text.

First release of AGrammarly.

• Three suggested replies for any message — casual, professional, short
• Matching runs on your device, with no network and no account
• Learns the phrases and emoji you actually use
• A practice keyboard with the suggestion bar, and a count of keystrokes saved
• Delete everything it has learned, in one action

review_information.notes:
Thanks for reviewing AGrammarly.

AGrammarly is an offline reply-suggestion app. No account, no sign-in, no network call and no in-app purchase — every feature is reachable on first launch, on a device in airplane mode. Suggestions are produced by pattern matching against a set that ships inside the binary (lib/core/engine/response_patterns.dart); there is no model and no server. This build defines no API_BASE_URL, so the cloud code path is unreachable and the Settings option for it is not shown. There is no advertising or analytics SDK. The app does not install a system keyboard: the Keyboard tab is a practice surface inside the app, which the listing states plainly.

Test instructions:
1. Launch the app and complete or skip onboarding. No account or permission is requested at any point.
2. On Home, type or paste an incoming message such as 'Are you free for lunch tomorrow?'. Three suggested replies appear, tagged casual, professional and short.
3. Tap a suggestion. The counters on Home increase - suggestions used, keystrokes saved, emoji - and the phrasing is folded into what the app has learned.
4. Open the Keyboard tab for the full QWERTY layout with the suggestion bar above it. Typing in the composer refreshes the chips; tapping one inserts it.
5. Open Settings. Suggestions run on-device and a line says so; there is no cloud option because this build has no endpoint configured.
6. Still in Settings, use 'Clear everything learned' to delete the stored style and counters, then return to Home to see the counters reset.
7. Turn on airplane mode and repeat any of the above - every feature still works, because nothing calls out.

Privacy:
• Data collected: The phrasings and emoji you use, learned from the replies you accept, plus three counters (suggestions used, keystrokes saved, emoji used). All of it is written to shared_preferences on your device.
• Network: None. The app makes no network request: this build defines no suggestions endpoint, so the cloud code path is unreachable and is not offered in Settings. Every feature works in airplane mode.
• Location: Not requested and not used.
• Tracking: None. There is no advertising SDK and no analytics SDK in the app, and it does not read the advertising identifier, so no App Tracking Transparency prompt appears.

If you need anything else, please email contact@safecodeg.com and we will respond within one business day.
